why_stage_2_failed.error: ValueError: duplicate seeds in [20260726, 20260726]; each seed counts once
why_stage_2_failed.root_cause: The frozen candidate universe is 5 searched leaves + 2 imported Phase-A finalists + 1 control = 8, and assumes those are DISTINCT. Because the search reproduced two of the imports exactly, two candidate ids each carry BOTH a cited historical sa probe (seed 20260726) and a newly run one at the same seed. Pooling refuses duplicate seeds — correctly, since counting one seed twice would inflate the evidence.
why_stage_2_failed.so_the_real_universe_was: 6 distinct candidates, not 8: 3 new leaves + 2 reproduced finalists + the control.
why_stage_2_failed.class: SCIENTIFIC/PROCEDURAL, not mechanical. The pooling guard did exactly its job; what is wrong is a preregistered candidate rule that cannot express 'a searched leaf turned out to BE an imported candidate'. Fixing it is a change to the frozen procedure and is a reviewer decision, not mine.
